input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: § 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment on us for three years expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — precisely the walk-away position under MINCOMMIT (multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right), and well short of the fallback (single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, trued up rather than penalised). It also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment, and § 7.1's prohibition on unidentified minimum-use charges. We therefore redline to the preferred position: no minimum commitment, with fees payable only for usage or ordered Services, and flag the 12-month/30-day-reduction true-up structure as the fallback if a commitment is commercially required.

proposal.summary: Remove the three-year take-or-pay minimum; fees payable for usage or ordered Services only
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a multi-year take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination right, so we have replaced it with payment for usage and ordered Services only — consistent with § 12.3, which already confirms we make no minimum-volume commitment. If Cobalt needs a commitment, we can discuss one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued up rather than penalised.

ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: Customer has no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment. Customer is obligated to pay only for Services it actually uses or orders under an executed Order Form.
